subject: Billing spike: proxy/API-key aggregation — request for usage re-attribution and credit
messages:
From: Infra Team <infra@novapps.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected billing spike — possible shared API key / proxy aggregation

Hi Soojin,

We're seeing a ~18x increase on invoice #2026-05-01 for our production account (NovaApps-main) compared to April. Our engineering team dug in and suspects several downstream services are routing through a shared API proxy that presents a single Redwood API key for multiple product instances. That would explain why the overage landed on the main account instead of being apportioned to the sub-accounts.

Can you: 1) provide a detailed usage export (per-request/attribution) for May, 2) confirm whether our requests were attributed to the API key or the per-subaccount keys, and 3) advise on options to split or re-attribute charges and any impact on tax/VAT? We need the breakdown for our procurement team to approve a reallocation and to reconcile with our internal billing.

Invoice attached for reference.

Attachments: [Attachment: invoice_2026-05-01.pdf (pdf, 120KB)]

Thanks — ideally we need a first pass within 48 hours so we can loop in finance.

— Infra Team
NovaApps Inc.
infra@novapps.com

On Fri, May 29, 2026 at 17:03, System Alert <alerts@novaapps.com> wrote:
> High request volume detected for API key: XXXX-XXXX. See: https://monitoring.novaapps.com/keys/XXXX-XXXX

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Infra Team <infra@novapps.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected billing spike — possible shared API key / proxy aggregation

Hi — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the invoice. We're opening this with Billing Ops immediately. I've looped in Ben (billing lead) and Marissa (account exec) so we can coordinate the usage export and next steps.

Immediate plan:
- Ben will pull a per-request export for May and a mapping table between API key -> account_id -> request_count.
- We'll validate whether attribution was made to the master API key vs child keys and confirm the scope of the overage.
- If re-attribution is required, we'll propose a remediation (split + credit) and include any tax/VAT implications.

For the export, can you confirm the list of sub-account IDs or any internal customer IDs that should be considered separate billable entities? That will help us match rows. If you prefer, we can accept a CSV of the internal mapping.

We will aim to deliver a first-pass analysis within 48 hours and a recommended resolution within 3 business days. We'll also pause automatic invoice collection for this invoice until we confirm the attribution — unless procurement asks otherwise.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Manager
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: internal_ticket_8421.txt]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 13:47:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Unexpected billing spike — possible shared API key / proxy aggregation

On Sat, May 30, 2026 at 10:05 AM Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> For the export, can you confirm the list of sub-account IDs or any internal customer IDs that should be considered separate billable entities?

Attached is a per-request sample export for May (first 100k lines) and a summarised attribution table. Key findings (quick summary):
1) Root cause: multiple downstream services were proxied through a single API key (XXXX-XXXX) belonging to NovaApps-main. The request logs show X-Account header present in ~73% of requests, but our billing attribution fell back to API key when explicit sub-account headers weren't provided by the proxy.
2) Volume: the overage portion (requests above your committed tier) maps to three internal product units: prod-search (34%), prod-notify (28%), prod-indexer (38%) by request count once we map X-Account values to your IDs.
3) Proposed remediation: re-attribute 100% of May's overage to the three internal units pro rata by request count and issue a one-time credit to NovaApps-main for the amount that should have been billed to those units.

Preliminary credit calculation (overage component only):
- Total overage charged on invoice: USD 10,890.50
- Pro-rata split -> prod-search (USD 3,712.77), prod-notify (USD 3,049.34), prod-indexer (USD 4,128.39)
- We propose issuing a credit of USD 8,890.50 against NovaApps-main and generating three internal charge-allocations for your finance ledger equal to the pro-rata amounts. The remaining USD 2,000 represents committed-tier reallocation (details in attached billing_note_draft).

Tax/VAT note: since your account is registered in the US (billing address on file), we will issue standard credit notes (no EU VAT reversal required). If any of the destination sub-accounts are EU-registered entities, we will need the VAT registration numbers to reissue invoices/credit notes appropriately — please confirm.

Timeline:
- Final validation & approval: 1 business day after you confirm sub-account IDs and VAT status.
- Credit processing and ledger adjustments: 3 business days.
- Funds reversal / payment system adjustments (if money moved): 7–10 business days depending on payment provider.

Attachments: [Attachment: usage_export_May2026.csv (csv, 1.2MB)], [Attachment: billing_note_draft.pdf (pdf, 45KB)]

Let me know if you want us to proceed with the re-attribution and credit. If you prefer a different split methodology (e.g., token-weighted instead of request-count), we can run that calc too — it changes the numbers by ~6–9%.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Billing Operations Lead, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Infra Team <infra@novapps.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: finance+procurement@novapps.com
Date: Sun, 31 May 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected billing spike — possible shared API key / proxy aggregation

Thanks Ben / Soojin — this all makes sense.

We confirm the mapping file is attached (internal_subaccount_map.csv) and none of the three destination product units are EU-registered; all are US entities under the NovaApps umbrella. Please proceed with the pro-rata re-attribution as you outlined and issue the credit note to NovaApps-main. Procurement asks that the internal charge allocations be provided as a CSV for our ledger ingestion.

Also please include a short line item in the credit note describing the root cause ("proxy presented shared API key; reattribution applied per internal X-Account header mapping") so our auditors have context.

If you can provide the final credit note and the CSV allocations by close of business Tuesday (2026-06-01), we can sign off and move the invoice hold to closed.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — copying finance.

— Infra Team
NovaApps Inc.
[Attachment: internal_subaccount_map.csv (csv, 3KB)]
